did_you_know.text: The verse addresses “all the earth” and calls it to sing a “new song” to the Lord; singing is thus presented as a universal call, not merely the act of one particular group.
The chapter connects blessing the Lord’s name with proclaiming his salvation every day: “Proclaim his salvation from day to day.”
The mission in this chapter is to tell the nations about the Lord’s glory and his wonders among all peoples—in other words, to spread knowledge of his deeds beyond Israel’s borders.
The Lord’s greatness is described through a series of words expressing praise and awe: he is “great,” “greatly to be praised,” and “to be feared above all gods.”
The verse contrasts the gods of the nations, called “idols,” with the Lord, of whom it says, “He made the heavens.” The power of creation serves here as a sign of the Lord’s uniqueness.
The word “Ascribe” is repeated three times in verses 7–8, emphasizing the call for the families of the nations to give the Lord glory, strength, and the glory due his name.
The proclamation of kingship, “The Lord reigns,” is linked to the world being firmly established and not moved, and to the Lord judging the peoples with equity.
The joy of the Lord’s reign is not limited to human beings: the heavens, the earth, the sea, and all that fills it are called to rejoice and shout for joy.
The fields and all the trees of the forest also join in the celebration; the chapter uses vivid, concrete imagery in which all creation becomes a participant in praise.
The chapter’s conclusion repeats the phrase “for he comes” twice and presents the Lord’s coming as a coming for judgment: he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with faithfulness.
